catalyst_text: Positive results and NDA Priority Review PDUFA 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: Pivotal Phase 2 Cohort 1 results in adolescents and adults with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva were presented at a scientific meeting, showing large reductions in new HO lesions and total lesion volume. The FDA accepted the NDA and granted Priority Review, setting a PDUFA target action date of 2026-09-26. These milestones advance the program toward potential approval in a rare disease with high unmet need.
catalyst_text_evidence: Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MIRM) and Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced pivotal Phase 2 results from Cohort 1 of the PROGRESS study evaluating zilurgisertib, an investigational oral activin receptor-like kinase 2 (ALK2) inhibitor, in adolescents and adults (≥12 years of age) with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Results were shared in a late-breaking rapid-fire presentation at ENDO 2026, the Endocrine Society's annual meeting. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted the New Drug Application (NDA) for zilurgisertib for the treatment of FOP in patients 12 years of age and older and granted Priority Review. The Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date for zilurgisertib is 2026-09-26.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 data at EHA congress
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 data in CALR‑mutant myelofibrosis showed rapid and durable improvements in spleen volume, symptoms, and anemia as monotherapy and with ruxolitinib. Safety was manageable with no dose‑limiting toxicities and high treatment continuation, supporting further development in MF.
catalyst_text_evidence: Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced updated clinical data from two Phase 1 studies evaluating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of INCA033989, a first-in-class mutant calreticulin (mutCALR)-targeted monoclonal antibody, in patients with mutCALR-expressing myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). These findings are being presented in oral and poster presentations at the European Hematology Association (EHA) 2026 Congress in Stockholm, Sweden (Session: Myeloproliferative neoplasms – Clinical, Presentation numbers: S216, PS1983, PF884). Results demonstrate that INCA033989 delivers broad, clinically meaningful improvements across spleen volume, symptom burden and anemia in patients with MF. No dose-limiting toxicities were observed, and a maximum tolerated dose was not reached.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 data and Breakthrough designation
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 results in essential thrombocythemia showed rapid, deep and durable hematologic responses with high CHR/PHR rates and correlated reductions in mutCALR VAF. The program also received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in 2025 for Type 1 CALR ET resistant or intolerant to cytoreductive therapy, underscoring potential clinical impact.
catalyst_text_evidence: In patients with ET, INCA033989 demonstrated rapid, deep and durable hematologic and molecular responses across both Type 1 and non-Type 1 CALR patients, supporting potential for disease modification in a population resistant or intolerant to prior cytoreductive therapy. Across doses, 70% (80/114) of patients achieved a complete hematologic response (CHR, platelet count ≤400 × 109/L and leukocytes <10 × 109/L) and 87% achieved complete or partial hematologic response (CHR/PHR, platelet count ≤600 × 109/L and leukocytes <10 × 109/L). In November of 2025, INCA033989 was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of patients with ET harboring a Type 1 CALR mutation who are resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy.

drug_indication: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma
catalyst_text: Phase 3 data showed improved progression free survival
detailed_catalyst_text: Pivotal Phase 3 frontMIND results showed that adding tafasitamab and lenalidomide to R-CHOP significantly improved progression-free survival versus R-CHOP in adults with previously untreated high-risk DLBCL or HGBL. Event-free survival was also significantly improved and overall survival trended favorably, underscoring the regimen’s potential impact in the first-line setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced positive results from the pivotal Phase 3 frontMIND trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of tafasitamab (Monjuvi®/Minjuvi®), a humanized Fc-modified cytolytic CD19-targeting monoclonal antibody, and lenalidomide added to R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone; Tafa-Len-R-CHOP) versus R-CHOP, the current standard of care, as a first-line treatment for adults with previously untreated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or high-grade B-cell lymphoma (HGBL). The results, which build on previously reported topline data and also recently announced at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology Annual Meeting, showed Tafa-Len-R-CHOP resulted in statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression-free survival (PFS). A 25% reduction in risk of disease progression or death demonstrated with Tafa-Len-R-CHOP compared with R-CHOP (HR 0.75 [P=0.0194]; 95% CI: 0.59, 0.96; median follow-up of 35.2 months). Tafa-Len-R-CHOP significantly improved event-free survival (EFS) compared to R-CHOP (HR 0.79 [P=0.0260] 95% CI: 0.64, 0.97; median follow-up of 35.4 months). Interim overall survival (OS) analysis demonstrated a positive trend toward improvement (HR=0.85 [P=0.2703] 95% CI: 0.63, 1.14, median follow-up of 35.9 months).

catalyst_text: NDA accepted under Priority Review PDUFA date set
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA for zilurgisertib in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva under Priority Review, establishing a PDUFA date of September 26, 2026. The submission was supported by pivotal Phase 2 PROGRESS study data. Priority Review signifies an expedited regulatory timeline for this ultra-rare disease therapy.
catalyst_text_evidence: The FDA has accepted the NDA for zilurgisertib in FOP under Priority Review with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of September 26, 2026. The late-breaking rapid-fire presentation will include results from Cohort 1 of the placebo-controlled PROGRESS study, which enrolled patients 12 years of age and older and formed the basis of the New Drug Application (NDA) for zilurgisertib to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

drug_indication: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma
catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 3 results meeting primary endpoint
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive Phase 3 frontMIND results in first-line high-risk diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and high-grade B-cell lymphoma showed a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival versus R-CHOP. Event-free survival was also significantly improved with supportive trends in overall survival, and the data were presented at ASCO with simultaneous publication in The Lancet. These outcomes underscore potential clinical benefit in this high-risk, previously untreated population.
catalyst_text_evidence: "Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced positive results from the pivotal Phase 3 frontMIND trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of tafasitamab (Monjuvi®/Minjuvi®) and lenalidomide added to R-CHOP ... versus R-CHOP alone as a first-line treatment for adults with previously untreated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or high-grade B-cell lymphoma (HGBL)." "The results build on previously reported topline data indicating the trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) by investigator assessment." "The data demonstrate that Tafa-Len-R-CHOP resulted in a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS, with a 25% reduction in risk of disease progression or death among patients treated with Tafa-Len-R-CHOP compared with R-CHOP alone (HR 0.75 [P=0.0194]; 95% CI, 0.59–0.96; median follow-up of 35.2 months)." "Treatment with Tafa-Len-R-CHOP also significantly improved the key secondary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) compared to R-CHOP alone (HR 0.79 [P=0.0260] 95% CI, 0.64-0.97; median follow-up of 35.4 months)." "The oral presentation of these data is taking place at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting ... with simultaneous publication in The Lancet*."

catalyst_text: Presented positive 24 week results and EU submission
detailed_catalyst_text: Final 24-week results from the Phase 3 TRuE-AD4 study in adults with moderate atopic dermatitis were presented at EADV, showing sustained disease control with high EASI75 and IGA-TS rates. The company also stated a Type‑II variation application was submitted in the EU for adults with moderate atopic dermatitis. This supports a potential label expansion in Europe, backed by new durability and safety data.
catalyst_text_evidence: "Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced final 24-week data from the Phase 3 TRuE-AD4 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of Opzelura® (ruxolitinib) cream in adults with moderate atopic dermatitis (AD) who had an inadequate response, intolerance or contraindication to topical corticosteroids (TCSs) and topical calcineurin inhibitors (TCIs)." "These data were presented (Abstract ID: P0851) today at the 2026 European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Symposium, being held 2026-05-07–2026-05-09, in Athens, Greece." "Data support Type-II variation application submitted for ruxolitinib cream 1.5% for the treatment of adults with moderate AD in the European Union (EU), feedback expected in 1H 2026." "Among those patients, 84.3% achieved EASI75 and 70.6% achieved IGA-TS at Week 24, similar to the frequencies at Week 8 (83.5% and 74.4%, respectively)."

catalyst_text: Received TGA approval for chronic graft-versus-host disease
detailed_catalyst_text: The therapy received Australian TGA approval for chronic graft-versus-host disease after failure of at least two prior systemic therapies in adults and paediatric patients 6 years and older weighing at least 40 kg. This regulatory milestone enables access to a new treatment option for patients with refractory disease in Australia.
catalyst_text_evidence: Specialised Therapeutics is pleased to announce that NIKTIMVO (axatilimab) has been approved for use in Australia by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for the treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and paediatric patients 6 years and older weighing at least 40 kg. NIKTIMVO was assessed through the TGA’s Priority Review pathway and is the first approved anti-colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (anti-CSF-1R) antibody for cGVHD.

drug_indication: Myelofibrosis, Polycythemia Vera, Acute Graft-Versus-Host Disease, Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease
catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for multiple hematologic disease indications
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved the extended-release, once-daily formulation for adults with intermediate- or high-risk myelofibrosis, adults with polycythemia vera after hydroxyurea failure, and patients 12 years and older with steroid-refractory acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease. This provides a new dosing option with exposure comparable to the immediate-release formulation, potentially improving treatment convenience.
catalyst_text_evidence: "Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Jakafi XR™ (ruxolitinib) extended-release tablets for the treatment of adults with intermediate- or high-risk myelofibrosis (MF); adults with polycythemia vera (PV) who have had an inadequate response to or are intolerant of hydroxyurea; as well as adults and children aged 12 years and older with steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or chronic GVHD after failure of one or two lines of systemic therapy."

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 3 results in first-line DLBCL
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive Phase 3 results from the pivotal frontMIND study in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma were reported. The data are slated for oral presentation at ASCO and are described as supportive of global regulatory submissions, indicating potential advancement toward filings.
catalyst_text_evidence: Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced that full results from the Phase 3 pivotal study evaluating tafasitamab (Monjuvi®/Minjuvi®) in first-line diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) will be featured as an oral presentation at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, to be held 2026-05-29 – 2026-06-02, in Chicago. “The positive Phase 3 frontMIND results for tafasitamab in patients with newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma highlight Incyte's continued focus on advancing novel differentiated approaches with the potential to meaningfully impact patients,” said Pablo J. Cagnoni, M.D., President and Global Head of Research and Development, Incyte.

drug_indication: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Anal Canal
catalyst_text: Received EC approval for first line advanced SCAC
detailed_catalyst_text: The European Commission approved retifanlimab in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic or inoperable locally recurrent squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal. This establishes the first systemic treatment option in Europe for this rare cancer and broadens available standard-of-care choices.
catalyst_text_evidence: Zynyz® (retifanlimab) in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel (platinum-based chemotherapy) is the first systemic treatment for adult patients with advanced SCAC in Europe. Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced that the European Commission (EC) has approved Zynyz® (retifanlimab) in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel (platinum-based chemotherapy) for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic or with inoperable locally recurrent squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC).

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 3 results meeting endpoint
detailed_catalyst_text: A pivotal Phase 3 study in first-line diffuse large B-cell lymphoma reported positive topline results, meeting the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed progression-free survival and the key secondary endpoint of event-free survival. These findings support the clinical benefit of adding the regimen to R-CHOP in newly diagnosed, higher-risk adults and may enable a future regulatory submission.
catalyst_text_evidence: Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced positive topline results from the pivotal Phase 3 frontMIND trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of tafasitamab (Monjuvi®/Minjuvi®), a humanized Fc-modified cytolytic CD19 targeting monoclonal antibody, and lenalidomide in addition to R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone) compared to R-CHOP alone as a first-line treatment for adults with newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of three to five (3-5) for patients >60 years of age, or age-adjusted IPI (aaIPI) of two to three (2-3) for patients ≤60 years of age. The trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) by investigator assessment (Hazard Ratio 0.75 [0.59,0.96]; p-value 0.019), according to Lugano 2014 criteria. The trial also met its key secondary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) by investigator assessment. No new safety signals were observed.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1 data and Breakthrough designation
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 data in essential thrombocythemia were presented, showing high rates of hematologic and molecular responses with a favorable safety profile. The FDA also granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for Type 1 CALR-mutant ET patients resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy, underscoring regulatory momentum.
catalyst_text_evidence: Incyte (NASDAQ:INCY) today announced updated clinical data from two Phase 1 studies evaluating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of INCA033989, a first-in-class mutant calreticulin (mutCALR)-targeted monoclonal antibody, as a treatment for patients with mutCALR-expressing myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). These data, which are featured in oral presentations at the 2025 American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting in Orlando (Session 634, Publication #1024; Session 631, Publication #71), focus on the dose escalation portion of the studies in patients with essential thrombocythemia (ET) harboring a CALR mutation who are resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation to INCA033989 for the treatment of patients with ET harboring a Type 1 CALR mutation who are resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy.
